stories.headline: Deaths of two US agents in Chihuahua drug lab operation ignite sovereignty crisis and federal-state conflict
stories.summary: Two US federal agents — reported by multiple outlets as CIA officers — died in a car crash during an anti-narcotics operation in Chihuahua that destroyed a drug lab. The incident triggered a week-long escalating dispute: Sheinbaum demanded explanations, accused Chihuahua governor Maru Campos of allowing unauthorized foreign agent participation, invoked Mexican sovereignty emphatically, and designated García Harfuch as the federal-state liaison. By Saturday April 25, the Security Cabinet confirmed neither agent had formal accreditation to participate in operations. The US, opposition parties (PAN, PRI), and US congressman McCaul pushed back on Sheinbaum's account.

stories.headline: Sheinbaum inaugurates Felipe Ángeles train linking Mexico City to AIFA airport
stories.summary: President Sheinbaum inaugurated the Felipe Ángeles suburban train connecting Buenavista station to the Felipe Ángeles International Airport (AIFA) on April 26, covering 41 km in under 60 minutes with an initial promotional fare of 45 pesos. Sheinbaum declared 'misión cumplida' at the ceremony, noting the project had been delayed but was now transferred to state operation after the private concession arrangement ended.

stories.headline: SEMAR contralmirante Fernando Farías Laguna arrested in Argentina on fuel-smuggling charges
stories.summary: Fernando Farías Laguna, a contralmirante in the Mexican Navy (SEMAR) and nephew of former SEMAR secretary Rafael Ojeda, was arrested in Buenos Aires on April 23-24 after entering Argentina on a false Guatemalan passport. He is accused of leading a network of 'huachicol fiscal' (hydrocarbon smuggling) through maritime customs. The Secretaría de Marina responded with a terse 'la ley es para todos' statement; Farías is seeking political asylum and his lawyers have implicated higher Navy commanders.

stories.headline: Morena leadership overhaul: Luisa Alcalde exits party presidency, Ariadna Montiel likely successor ahead of 2027 elections
stories.summary: President Sheinbaum engineered a restructuring of Morena's national leadership, effectively pushing out party president Luisa María Alcalde (who will move to the Consejería Jurídica) and signaling Ariadna Montiel (Bienestar secretary) and Citlalli Hernández for the top two party positions. Morena's National Council is convened for May 3 to formalize the transition. The move is widely read as Sheinbaum consolidating direct control over the party ahead of 17 gubernatorial contests in 2027.
